_: The Jonson surfacing suite. One entry per scenario; a scenario is one or more turns in
ONE fresh conversation (same cid and cookie jar, continuation=1 from the second turn).
Each turn names the surfaces it EXPECTS (must appear) and FORBIDS (must not appear).
Surfaces are the SSE event names the ask endpoint emits: context (the photo rail),
casestudies, clients, sectors, method, testimonial, contact, music, suggestions.
Expectations are PRODUCT intent — what the answer should carry — never a description of
how the current code behaves. A surface not listed either way is a don't-care.
Run: node tools/jonson/run.mjs [runs=6] [concurrency=4] [filter]
`singleTestimonial` on a scenario: any testimonial panel shown in it must carry exactly one quote (no `has-multiple`).
`maxStudies: N` on a turn: the casestudies panel, if shown, carries at most N cards.
`maxWords: N` on a turn: the answer's prose (markers stripped) is at most N words — a card on screen means a lead-in, not an essay.
`noRepeatStudies` on a turn: no case-study card in it was already on screen earlier in the conversation. The twin of noRepeatPhotos.
`noWorkChip` on a turn: no chip it offers is a generic 'can I see your work?' — the assertion for a chip that leads nowhere.
`tap: n` on a turn REPLACES its `q` with the nth chip the previous turn offered (0 by default). A scenario that taps cannot know what it
will ask, which is the point: the assertion is about where a chip LEADS, and that has to hold whatever the model chose to write.

_: The incident: work goes on screen, the conversation widens, and a later ask for the work brings back a second
strip carrying the first one's cards. Turn 1 puts the cards up so the rest cannot pass vacuously; turn 2 widens
the way the real conversation did; turn 3 asks the generic question that every chip filter lets through, because
it names no study and says 'projects' rather than 'case studies'.
Turn 1 asks NARROW on purpose. Open with 'show me your work' and all seven cards go up, after which every later
ask is correctly skipped for having nothing new — the scenario passes having tested only the easy case.

_: The same defect reached the way a visitor actually reaches it — by tapping. A scenario that taps cannot know
what it will ask, which is the point: WHEREVER the chips lead, they must not lead back to what is already on
screen. This is the only scenario in the suite that travels the route the suggestion layer chooses.
Narrow opener, for the same reason work-repeat has one: a full catalogue on turn 1 makes the rest unfalsifiable.
